---
title: "Overview of Ecosystem Service: Moisture Recycling (Rainfall Pattern Regulation)"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    standalone: true
---

Rainfall pattern regulation values the part of the crop rent attributed to vegetation-derived
moisture: Shunkei's VMR coefficients applied to the 2019 commercial crop-provision values in the
water_supply run, and reported AT THE RECEIVING COUNTRY, the agreed paper approach. The base
year is 2019.

⚠ The published headline is an **intermediate contribution already inside crop provision, never
an addition to it**, the same convention as agricultural water, whose basis it shares. It also
overlaps agricultural water itself, because the VMR value is part of the green-water value.
The earlier construction (the water-supply irrigation and domestic GEP re-attributed to
supplying countries) is RETIRED and is not published under any name.

## Quantity

Shunkei's VMR coefficients, from his pinned pipeline (`Shunkei3/GEP-WaterUse-Agriculture` at
`e229f881`, Code/3 lines 146-212). For each crop and country, the green water that satisfied
the crop's requirement is split, grid cell by grid cell, into a part that originated as
vegetation moisture recycling (VMR) and a non-VMR part, using his VMR grid table.
`lambda_gn_rf_vmr` and `lambda_gn_ir_vmr` are then the Ky-weighted means, over growth stages, of
the VMR-origin green-water satisfaction ratios on rainfed and on irrigated production.

They are biophysical ratios, not water volumes and not shares of value. Applying them to a
monetary value attributes that value in proportion, an assumption the method shares with
agricultural water, not a measured rent.

## Price

The basis is the account's 2019 commercial crop-provision value, the crop rent (FAOSTAT gross
production value times CWoN's cropland rental rate), split into rainfed and irrigated parts by
SPAM's production shares. It is not gross crop output. The water_supply run computes the two
components, `lambda_gn_rf_vmr` times the rainfed basis and `lambda_gn_ir_vmr` times the
irrigated basis, and publishes them by receiving country as `water_use_rainfed_vmr_gep` and
`water_use_irrigated_vmr_gep`.

This service reads them from the LIVE water table: an explicit `moisture_recycling_water_gep_path`
wins, else `moisture_recycling_water_gep_relative_file` against the project directory, so the
figure is as fresh as the last water_supply run and a stale copy cannot shadow it. The resolved
path is pinned before the reuse decision, so a new water table invalidates the saved result. The
component columns are configuration (`moisture_recycling_water_gep_component_cols`).

## Valuation

The headline, `moisture_recycling_gep`, is the receiving country's two VMR components summed,
a country missing both staying missing. It does not use the WAM2layers matrix.

## Coverage

The published table is one row for each of the account's 250 countries, base year 2019, in
constant 2019 USD. Of the 250, 158 carry a value and 92 are missing, kept as missing rather
than zero. The VMR pair is a subset of the agricultural water coverage (164), because six of
its countries (BHS, CYP, JAM, MLT, PRI, TTO) carry lambda components with no VMR observation.
A zero means the computation returned zero, and a missing row means the data to compute one is
absent. The headline equals the water table's two VMR columns summed per country, to within
$1.2e-7 per country, with identical missing values.

## Source-side diagnostic (WAM2layers), not the headline

Beside the headline the task publishes a diagnostic: where the land-sourced part of that value
would sit if it were credited to the countries whose evaporation supplied the rain.

It uses the WAM2layers country-to-country sink-fraction matrix (Bakels and Wang-Erlandsson):
cell $[i, j]$ is the fraction of column-country $j$'s 2019 precipitation that evaporated from
row-country $i$'s land. A column sums to $j$'s terrestrial-origin share, below one because the
remainder comes from the ocean. The matrix is read from `moisture_recycling_sink_fraction_input_path`.

$$
\text{source}_i = s \sum_j M_{ij} \, V_j
$$

where $V_j$ is destination $j$'s headline value and $s$ is `moisture_recycling_ecosystem_share`,
the share of terrestrial evaporation credited to ecosystems. It is 1 in `es_parameters.csv`, and
the transpiration-share decision that would lower it is open with the group. The diagonal term
is the own part (a country's moisture serving its own crops), the rest the export part, and the
destination-side view is published as `moisture_recycling_sink_side_value`.

Three things affect the diagnostic only, never the headline:

- countries carrying a VMR value but absent from the matrix, which it cannot place;
- twelve destinations below the 0.5 degree tracking grid, whose matrix columns are all missing;
- the ecosystem share $s$.

Because the matrix columns sum below one, the diagnostic total is the land-sourced part of the
headline, not the headline. The task checks that the source-side and destination-side totals of
the diagnostic agree. That is one double sum computed two ways, not a conservation of the
headline, so the diagnostic is not an allocation of the full headline value.

## Inputs

All paths and parameters come from `es_parameters.csv` under the `moisture_recycling` service
key: the water-supply table, the component column list, the sink-fraction matrix and the
ecosystem share, each with a source row beside it.

## Taken as given

Shunkei's VMR coefficients and his VMR grid table, at `e229f881`. Their derivation (his
Code/3) is not reproduced here.

## Against the authors' write-up

The authors' rainfall write-up (28 October 2026: Sylla, Kakimoto, Ren, Bakels, Wang
Erlandsson) matches this implementation's structure: the same VMR green-water coefficients on
the SPAM-split crop basis, summed at the receiving country, reported as an intermediate
contribution and never added, with transboundary attribution out of scope.

Shunkei, who owns the shared pipeline, settled two earlier questions on 28 October 2026. The
intended monetary base is commercial crop-provision value, and only FAOSTAT's Wheat and Millet
items are divided among several crop categories, with no other group allocation. The account
also removes FAOSTAT's group totals. His revised code is not yet published (his repository's
main is still `e229f881`), so the library matches his stated intended method, and the revised
code itself has not been checked.

What remains specific to rainfall is the write-up's wording. It still calls the crop input the
gross farm-gate production value and describes SPAM allocation of crop groups, so its authors
need to confirm the commercial crop-provision base and bring the text into line.
